investigation.title: Remote Agents: Swarm Gateway 502 Blocking All Agent Provisioning Evals (production-api)
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents feature checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-08-28T03:23:18Z with an identical 502 bad_gateway error indicating the swarm provisioning gateway — an AWS ELB in us-east-2 — was unreachable when POST /api/agents was called. Because the failure occurs before any agent is created, zero required evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected, and all contract assertions are unverifiable.
investigation.rootCause: The swarm gateway (an AWS ELB endpoint in us-east-2 serving /v1/agents) was unreachable at the time of the eval run. The production-api layer returned HTTP 502 with code "bad_gateway" and the message "swarm gateway unreachable during agent provisioning: error sending request for url (http://[REDACTED].elb.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/v1/agents)" for every attempt. This is an infrastructure-layer failure localized to the swarm gateway dependency, not to the eval runner or its configuration. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact is scoped to this observability eval run.

possibleCauses: The AWS ELB serving the swarm /v1/agents endpoint in us-east-2 was down, misconfigured, or had no healthy targets at the time of the eval run — the most strongly supported cause given the identical 502 across all three sibling checks
A transient network partition or DNS resolution failure between the production-api layer and the ELB prevented the connection from being established
The swarm service behind the ELB crashed or was restarted, causing the ELB to return 502 while targets were unhealthy

A deployment or configuration change to the swarm gateway or its ELB target group rendered it temporarily unreachable — no suspect changes are listed in sourceDiscovery.suspectChanges, so this remains a lower-confidence hypothesis

investigation.title: Remote Agents: Swarm Gateway 502 Blocking All Agent Provisioning Evals (production-api)
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed simultaneously in production-api with an identical 502 bad_gateway error indicating the swarm ELB endpoint at /v1/agents was unreachable during agent provisioning. Because the failure occurs at the POST /api/agents call before any agent identity is returned, zero required evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was collected, causing a complete contract gap for the remote-agent-state eval.
investigation.rootCause: The swarm gateway — an AWS ELB in us-east-2 fronting the /v1/agents provisioning endpoint — was unreachable at the time of the eval run (2026-08-28T03:23:29–03:23:51Z). Every remote-agents check that calls POST /api/agents received HTTP 502 with error code bad_gateway and the message "swarm gateway unreachable during agent provisioning." Because agent creation is the first step in the remote-agent-state probe (run-status-probes.mjs line 1905: createAgent(args, track, "remote", null, orgId)), the probe never advanced past provisioning, leaving all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) absent. This is an eval-infrastructure failure against the production-api swarm gateway; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: Primary: The AWS ELB backing the swarm /v1/agents endpoint was down, misconfigured, or had no healthy targets at the time of the eval run, causing the production-api gateway to return 502 for all agent provisioning requests.

Secondary: A network routing or security-group change between the production-api service and the swarm ELB in us-east-2 blocked outbound connections to the ELB, producing a connection error surfaced as 502.
Tertiary: The swarm service itself (behind the ELB) was restarting or had crashed, causing the ELB to report no healthy backends and return 502 to the production-api caller.

investigations.summary: All three remote-agents feature checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-08-28T03:23:18Z with an identical 502 bad_gateway error indicating the swarm provisioning gateway — an AWS ELB in us-east-2 — was unreachable when POST /api/agents was called. Because the failure occurs before any agent is created, zero required evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected, and all contract assertions are unverifiable.
investigations.rootCause: The swarm gateway (an AWS ELB endpoint in us-east-2 serving /v1/agents) was unreachable at the time of the eval run. The production-api layer returned HTTP 502 with code "bad_gateway" and the message "swarm gateway unreachable during agent provisioning: error sending request for url (http://[REDACTED].elb.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/v1/agents)" for every attempt. This is an infrastructure-layer failure localized to the swarm gateway dependency, not to the eval runner or its configuration. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact is scoped to this observability eval run.

recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Directly verifies whether the ELB has healthy targets registered for /v1/agents. An empty or all-unhealthy target group would confirm the gateway was down at eval time.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Query production-api logs for POST /api/agents errors in the 03:23 UTC window on 2026-08-28
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Determines whether the 502 originated from a failed outbound TCP connection, a DNS resolution error, or an HTTP-level rejection from the ELB, which narrows the infrastructure layer responsible.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If a direct HTTP request to the swarm gateway ELB /v1/agents endpoint succeeds with 200 at the time of re-run, the gateway itself is not down and the failure may be isolated to the production-api's routing or credential configuration.
If only remote-agent-runtime fails while remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state pass on re-run, the failure is not a shared gateway outage but is specific to the runtime eval path.

If the production-api logs show the outbound request to the ELB was never attempted (e.g., DNS failure before TCP connect), the root cause is a DNS or network configuration issue rather than ELB target health.
If the ELB target group shows all targets InService and the /v1/agents route is healthy, the 502 may have been a transient spike rather than a sustained gateway outage.
If no-history data (previousRunCount=0) is explained by this being the first eval run, a passing result on immediate re-run would indicate a transient fault rather than a persistent gateway failure.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated swarm-gateway-health eval that directly probes the ELB /v1/agents endpoint (or a lightweight health route) independently of the full agent provisioning flow, so gateway-level failures are surfaced before the agent creation step is attempted.

Add a pre-flight connectivity check in the remote-agent-create probe that distinguishes a gateway-unreachable 502 from an application-level provisioning error, enabling faster triage of infrastructure vs. application failures.

Once a passing baseline is established, configure history tracking (previousRunCount > 0) so that currentlyRegressedFromPass can be computed and regressions from a known-good state are flagged automatically.

Add a sibling-correlation eval that fires an explicit alert when all checks under a feature share the same failure message, confirming shared-dependency failures without requiring manual cross-check of sibling results.
